name: Tainted Tablet

angles.text: The Tainted Tablet marks the formal introduction of fledgling warlocks in Durotar to their trainer, Nartok, urging them to master the Nether rather than fear it.
Given the catastrophic legacy of demonic pacts on Draenor, practicing fel magic remains controversial among orcs, forcing Durotar's warlocks to counsel secrecy and boldness.
While Thrall's new Horde is wary of demonic corruption, practitioners lurking in places like the Den claim they can safely command Nether powers to secure a future for their people.

faq.answer: The Tainted Tablet is a written summons delivered to an aspiring practitioner in the Valley of Trials. It instructs them to seek out Nartok, their class trainer, who awaits inside the Den.
The tablet was sent by Nartok, an orc warlock trainer stationed inside the Den in the Valley of Trials. He uses it to introduce himself to newly arrived practitioners and invite them for instruction.
Nartok resides inside the Den, a cavern tucked away in the Valley of Trials where darker arts and specialized training are practiced out of sight.

Nartok cautions that ordinary folk fear powers they do not understand, often lashing out in panic. Because the orcs suffered deeply under demonic corruption in their past, warlocks keep their arts guarded and tread cautiously.
faq.q: Why does Nartok warn to guard your powers closely?

faq.answer: Nartok believes that where conventional leaders falter, those who master the entities of the Nether can forge their own path and seize power to shape their people's destiny rather than be enslaved by it.
faq.q: What is Nartok's view on practicing fel magic?

faq.answer: A local questgiver in the Valley of Trials passes the tablet along, openly admitting discomfort with fel spellcasters but acknowledging the necessity of delivering Nartok's summons.
faq.q: Who gives you the Tainted Tablet?

sections.body: The Tainted Tablet is an inscribed message delivered to newly arrived practitioners beginning their journey in the Valley of Trials. Passing through the hands of uneasy camp caretakers, the stone bears a summons from Nartok, a warlock trainer making his home within the shadowed recesses of the Den. The missive invites the reader to step away from ordinary tribal duties and explore the deeper, forbidden currents of magic.
sections.title: A Dark Summons

sections.body: Upon answering the summons, Nartok speaks frankly about the turbulent history between orcs and the Nether. Rather than renouncing these volatile energies out of shame or fear, he argues that the strong must seize command of their own destiny. In his eyes, where conventional chieftains falter, practitioners who harness Nether entities with cunning will rise to prominence. However, because fearful minds readily strike out at what they do not comprehend, he warns that such powers must always be guarded closely.
sections.title: Commanding the Nether

summary: The Tainted Tablet is a starter quest in the Valley of Trials that directs aspiring spellcasters to Nartok inside the Den. It introduces the pragmatic yet cautious mindset of Durotar's warlocks, who seek to harness the Nether to forge their own destiny despite the lingering stigma of their past.
